gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the Fosi Audio M03 (the sub amp Dealectric lists, $76.49 today) is rated only for 4–8 Ω loads, so it cannot drive a 2 Ω subwoofer or a dual-voice-coil sub wired to 2 Ω. The 2 Ω-rated choices among the candidates are Fosi's own M01-BT (2–8 Ω) or the Behringer NX3000D (2 x 1,500 W at 2 Ω).
standout_why: The two cited rivals are B&H compare pages (EPQ304 / XLS1002 / NX3000D / A800, and NX3000D vs XLS1502). Both returned HTTP 403 to me, so I am judging from their titles and from ChatGPT's answer, which cites them. Those pages cover only Behringer and Crown rack amps. The Sweetwater results are category listings, ChurchSoundCalc covers church PA, and the B&H PDFs are 2015 and 2019 catalogs. None of these covers the Fosi M03, the M01-BT or the Dayton SPA250DSP, so none can give their load ranges. ChatGPT itself only says 'match the amplifier to the subwoofer's 2Ω, 4Ω, or 8Ω load' and never gives a limit for any amp. The B&H spec tables probably do list Crown and Behringer power at each load, so the rack-amp half of the finding is likely already covered there.
decides: The pick depends on the sub's impedance. For a 4 Ω or 8 Ω passive home sub fed from an AVR's RCA sub out, the Fosi M03 works ($76.49, RCA in, 20–200 Hz low-pass), but Fosi says the supplied 32 V/5 A brick does not reach rated maximum power (DC input goes up to 48 V). For a 2 Ω load, rule out the M03 and the Dayton SPA250DSP (rated only into 4 Ω). Pick the Fosi M01-BT (2–8 Ω, $89.99) or the NX3000D in stereo mode (2 x 1,500 W at 2 Ω, $339). The NX3000D is rated down to 4 Ω when bridged. The Dayton SPA250DSP is a plate amp that needs a 9.25 x 6.25 in cutout in the sub's cabinet, so it only suits DIY enclosures you can cut. The Crown XLS 1002 is the only rack candidate whose maker page I opened that lists RCA inputs (alongside XLR and 1/4 in), so it connects directly to an AVR sub out.
